I was shocked to learn recently that some scientists want to scale back their research in an effort to decrease carbon emissions. The crisis is here, they said, and we need to cut back on our energy-intensive modelling. At the very least, we need to make our energy use far more sustainable.

It is unarguable that our laboratories, scientific instruments, rockets and satellites — the tools we scientists need to measure the planet’s pulse — demand significant amounts of energy both in their construction and operation. And it is equally true that science’s unrelenting appetite for information has caused a mushrooming of energy-intensive data centres around the world. According to the International Energy Agency, these buildings now consume about 1 per cent of the world’s electricity.

However, this is a price we must pay for understanding the world. How can we inform decision makers about the best ways to bring down carbon emissions if we can’t track the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, where it’s coming from and who’s producing it? The carbon emissions from technological research are well spent: ultimately this research will safeguard the future of our planet.

It can be hard for scientists to make the case because our work is complex, often takes place behind closed doors and does not always lend itself to easy interpretation or explanation. But demonstrating the efficacy of science will be crucial if we are to solve humanity’s greatest challenges. It is all too easy to feel paralysed in the face of daunting problems such as climate change and to do nothing. But then I think of a friend’s daughter who turned her fears into action: she became a wind energy engineer and now thrives on delivering renewable energy, limiting emissions.

Recognising the hope that science and engineering can bring was the impetus behind the creation of the Millennium Technology Prize, which is now entering its 20th year as a celebration of human ingenuity. One of the past winners, Professor Martin Green from the University of New South Wales, Australia, is the inventor of the Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell technology which is now found in most of the world’s solar panels. Thanks to his invention, we have a real chance to decrease the world’s carbon emissions.

Every day, scientists, technologists and engineers are discovering new ways to exploit renewable energy sources and develop techniques not just to use power more intelligently but to power our intelligence. A great example of this is Europe’s largest supercomputer, LUMI in Finland, which is astonishingly carbon-negative. Established in an old paper mill, it is powered by a nearby river and its remote heat warms the people who live in the surrounding town of Kajaani.

If the world is to meet its net-zero ambitions, we must think hard about how we can deliver sustainable computing and deliver more LUMIs.

接下来看这句话到底说了什么：作者惊讶地发现，一些科学家竟然打算缩减自己的研究工作，目的是为了减少碳排放。注意这里的want to scale back their research，意思就是“有意减少研究活动”。而选项[B]说的正是“intention to reduce their research”，其中intention to对应原文的want to，reduce也和scale back意思一致，完全匹配。

It is unarguable that our laboratories, scientific instruments, rockets and satellites — the tools we scientists need to measure the planet’s pulse — demand significant amounts of energy both in their construction and operation. And it is equally true that science’s unrelenting appetite for information has caused a mushrooming of energy-intensive data centres around the world. According to the International Energy Agency, these buildings now consume about 1 per cent of the world’s electricity.

However, this is a price we must pay for understanding the world. How can we inform decision makers about the best ways to bring down carbon emissions if we can’t track the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, where it’s coming from and who’s producing it? The carbon emissions from technological research are well spent: ultimately this research will safeguard the future of our planet.

It can be hard for scientists to make the case because our work is complex, often takes place behind closed doors and does not always lend itself to easy interpretation or explanation. But demonstrating the efficacy of science will be crucial if we are to solve humanity’s greatest challenges. It is all too easy to feel paralysed in the face of daunting problems such as climate change and to do nothing. But then I think of a friend’s daughter who turned her fears into action: she became a wind energy engineer and now thrives on delivering renewable energy, limiting emissions.

Recognising the hope that science and engineering can bring was the impetus behind the creation of the Millennium Technology Prize, which is now entering its 20th year as a celebration of human ingenuity. One of the past winners, Professor Martin Green from the University of New South Wales, Australia, is the inventor of the Passivated Emitter and Rear Cell technology which is now found in most of the world’s solar panels. Thanks to his invention, we have a real chance to decrease the world’s carbon emissions.

Every day, scientists, technologists and engineers are discovering new ways to exploit renewable energy sources and develop techniques not just to use power more intelligently but to power our intelligence. A great example of this is Europe’s largest supercomputer, LUMI in Finland, which is astonishingly carbon-negative. Established in an old paper mill, it is powered by a nearby river and its remote heat warms the people who live in the surrounding town of Kajaani.

If the world is to meet its net-zero ambitions, we must think hard about how we can deliver sustainable computing and deliver more LUMIs.

题干中提供的定位信息有限，可以从以下两个方面考虑缩小定位区间：

①根据考研命题的题文同序原则，第 29 题的定位点主要出现在6段，由此可推断，本题应该与7段有关；

②根据本题的提问方式：作者同意以下哪项表述，可知该题询问作者的观点，所以可适当结合全文，宏观考虑本文中心主旨。

7段指出：如果全世界要实现净零目标，我们必须认真思考如何实现可持续计算并生产更多的 LUMI 计算机（If the world is to meet its net-zero ambitions, we must think hard about how we can deliver sustainable computing and deliver more LUMIs）。

由此可知，想要减少碳排放，就要进行更多的科研来实现可持续计算。并且，作者在3段已表明立场：科研工作产生的碳排放是我们了解世界必须付出的代价（However, this is a price we must pay for understanding the world）。以上两点表达了作者对未来科研工作的期望，也呼应了文章中心主旨选项 [C] 中 Energy-intensive research（能源密集型研究）是对文中反复提到的耗能巨大的科研工作的同义替换，inevitable（必不可少的）对应作者的核心观点 “这是必须付出的代价”（this is a price we must pay）。

这道题问的是“作者会同意以下哪一项说法”，也就是说，我们要找的是和作者观点一致的选项。这类题目不能光看一句话，得结合上下文甚至全文的立场来判断。


首先，根据考研阅读的一个小技巧——题文同序原则，上一题（第29题）的答案大概率出现在第6段，那这道题就很有可能在第7段附近找线索。果不其然，第7段开头就有一句关键话：“If the world is to meet its net-zero ambitions, we must think hard about how we can deliver sustainable computing and deliver more LUMIs.” 这句话的意思是：如果全球真想实现碳中和目标，就必须认真思考如何做到可持续计算，并造出更多像LUMI这样的超级计算机。注意这里的“must”——语气很坚决，说明作者认为这类高能耗的科研计算虽然耗能，但非做不可。


再往前翻，第3段其实已经埋下了作者的态度：“However, this is a price we must pay for understanding the world.” 意思是，科研带来的碳排放，是我们认识世界必须付出的代价。这里的“must pay”和第7段的“must think hard”形成呼应，说明作者并不反对高能耗科研，而是认为它虽然有环境代价，但不可避免、值得承担。


现在看选项，正确答案应该体现出“能源密集型研究虽然耗能，但必不可少”这个意思。而选项[C]中的“Energy-intensive research is inevitable”正好精准对应了这一点——“inevitable”就是“不可避免的”，和原文“a price we must pay”完全匹配。这里要注意一个常见陷阱：有些同学看到“energy-intensive”就本能觉得是负面词，但作者的态度恰恰是接受甚至支持这种研究，关键在于理解上下文的情感倾向，而不是孤立看词汇本身。


所以，解这类观点题，不能只盯着一个词或一句话，要抓住作者反复强调的立场。同时，留意像must, have to, inevitable, necessary这类表达“必要性”的词，它们往往是作者态度的信号灯。

Ever since taking on Netflix Inc. at its own game, old Hollywood has struggled to turn a profit in streaming, with the likes of Disney+, Peacock and Paramount+ losing billions of dollars each year, sparking concerns that the services will never be as profitable as cable once was. But the age of streaming has been a boon for some unintended winners: pirates that use software to rip a film or television show in seconds from legitimate online video platforms and host the titles on their own, illegitimate services, which rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions.

With no video production costs, illegal streaming sites have achieved profit margins approaching 90%, according to the Motion Picture Association (MPA), a trade group representing Hollywood studios that’s working to crack down on the thousands of illegal platforms that have cropped up in recent years.

Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads. But now piracy involving illegal streaming services as well as file-sharing costs the US economy about $30 billion in lost revenue a year and some 250,000 jobs, estimates the US Chamber of Commerce's Global Innovation Policy Center. The global impact is about $71 billion annually.

“The people who are stealing our movies and our television shows and operating piracy sites are not mom and pop operations,” says Charlie Rivkin, chief executive officer of the MPA. “This is organized crime.” Rivkin joined the MPA in 2017 after the organization failed five years earlier to build consensus between Hollywood and Silicon Valley to win passage of legislation in Congress aimed at stopping online piracy. In 2017, the association formed the Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE), an enforcement task force of about 100 detectives circling the globe to help local authorities arrest streaming pirates.

ACE says it’s helped shrink the number of illegal streaming services in North America to 126, from more than 1,400 in 2018, aided in part by the MPA’s support for a 2020 federal law that made large-scale streaming of copyrighted material a serious crime.

Consulting firm Parks Associates predicts that legitimate US streaming services cumulative loss from piracy since 2022 will reach $113 billion in the next two years. “While there is some optimism that emerging countermeasures and best practices may see piracy begin to plateau by 2027, there is no consensus among stakeholders as to when it may begin to decline,” says analyst Steve Hawley.
2025-Traditional Reading-3-1.analysis:
根据题干中的关键词 Paragraph 1 和 legitimate streaming services 可定位至文章1段。该段由两句话构成，1句与2句之间通过连词 But 连接，表达转折逻辑。在这种情况下，核心信息往往位于2句，需多加留意。

1段1句：该句介绍了传统好莱坞影业在流媒体业务上一直难以盈利（old Hollywood has struggled to turn a profit in streaming）。

1段2句：该句转折指出，一些盗版商（pirates）反而通过从合法视频平台盗取电影或电视节目获取了巨额利润（rake in about $2 billion annually）。

综上可知，选项[D] are confronted with a real threat（正面临着真正的威胁）是对1段1句中的old Hollywood has struggled to turn a profit in streaming和2句中的pirates以及rake in about $2 billion annually 的合理概括。
2025-Traditional Reading-3-1.tips:
这道题问的是第一段提到“合法流媒体服务”时，作者想表达什么意思。我们先别急着看选项，而是回到原文第一段，看看作者到底说了啥。


第一段开头说，传统好莱坞在流媒体业务上一直很难赚钱（old Hollywood has struggled to turn a profit in streaming）。这句话其实已经点出了一个困境：明明是正规军，却赚不到钱。紧接着，作者用了一个But，引出下一句——盗版商反而每年靠偷这些平台的内容狂赚20亿美元（pirates rake in about $2 billion annually by stealing movies and TV shows from legitimate streaming services）。


注意这里有个很关键的对比逻辑：正规平台亏钱，盗版团伙却大把捞钱。这种反差说明，盗版不是小打小闹，而是对合法流媒体构成了实实在在的冲击。所以作者提到“合法流媒体服务”，其实是在强调它们正面临一个严重且真实的威胁。


很多同学容易掉进一个陷阱：看到“struggled to turn a profit”就以为问题出在商业模式本身，比如成本太高、用户太少等等。但千万别忽略后半句！But后面才是重点——作者真正想说的是，**盗版行为加剧了这个困境**，甚至成了压垮盈利的关键因素之一。


所以正确答案要能体现出“外部威胁”这个意思。选项[D] “are confronted with a real threat”（正面临真正的威胁）正好抓住了这个核心。它没具体说是什么威胁，但结合上下文，显然指的就是那些靠偷内容年入20亿的盗版者。

这道题问的是 Hawley 对数字隐私（digital privacy）问题的看法，但其实文章里提到 Hawley 的地方，并不是在讨论隐私本身，而是借他之口谈盗版问题的发展趋势。所以第一步要做的，就是别被“digital privacy”这个关键词带偏了方向——它只是话题背景，真正要关注的是 Hawley 到底说了什么。

Ever since taking on Netflix Inc. at its own game, old Hollywood has struggled to turn a profit in streaming, with the likes of Disney+, Peacock and Paramount+ losing billions of dollars each year, sparking concerns that the services will never be as profitable as cable once was. But the age of streaming has been a boon for some unintended winners: pirates that use software to rip a film or television show in seconds from legitimate online video platforms and host the titles on their own, illegitimate services, which rake in about $2 billion annually from ads and subscriptions.

With no video production costs, illegal streaming sites have achieved profit margins approaching 90%, according to the Motion Picture Association (MPA), a trade group representing Hollywood studios that’s working to crack down on the thousands of illegal platforms that have cropped up in recent years.

Initially the rise of legitimate online businesses such as Netflix actually helped curb digital piracy, which had largely been based on file uploads. But now piracy involving illegal streaming services as well as file-sharing costs the US economy about $30 billion in lost revenue a year and some 250,000 jobs, estimates the US Chamber of Commerce's Global Innovation Policy Center. The global impact is about $71 billion annually.

“The people who are stealing our movies and our television shows and operating piracy sites are not mom and pop operations,” says Charlie Rivkin, chief executive officer of the MPA. “This is organized crime.” Rivkin joined the MPA in 2017 after the organization failed five years earlier to build consensus between Hollywood and Silicon Valley to win passage of legislation in Congress aimed at stopping online piracy. In 2017, the association formed the Alliance for Creativity and Entertainment (ACE), an enforcement task force of about 100 detectives circling the globe to help local authorities arrest streaming pirates.

ACE says it’s helped shrink the number of illegal streaming services in North America to 126, from more than 1,400 in 2018, aided in part by the MPA’s support for a 2020 federal law that made large-scale streaming of copyrighted material a serious crime.

Consulting firm Parks Associates predicts that legitimate US streaming services cumulative loss from piracy since 2022 will reach $113 billion in the next two years. “While there is some optimism that emerging countermeasures and best practices may see piracy begin to plateau by 2027, there is no consensus among stakeholders as to when it may begin to decline,” says analyst Steve Hawley.
2025-Traditional Reading-3-5.analysis:
根据题干中的关键词 is emphasized in the text 可知本题属于主旨题的类型，需结合文章整体结构，判断本篇文章所强调的内容。

文中1-2段：说明了非法流媒体盗版的猖獗。影视公司处于盈利困境（has struggled to turn a profit in streaming），而非法流媒体平台通过窃取合法平台的内容赚取巨额利润（rake in about $2 billion annually）。这一对比直观地突出了合法与非法流媒体在盈利方面的巨大反差。

3段：阐述了盗版现象产生的严重危害，指出盗版行为给美国造成了巨大的经济损失，还导致工作岗位的流失（costs the US economy about $30 billion in lost revenue a year and some 250,000 jobs）。

4-5段：介绍了为整治影视盗版行为所做的尝试与取得的成果。

6段：对打击盗版的未来成效进行预测：虽然目前小有进展，短期内能够遏制增长势头，但这项任务道阻且长。

综上分析可知，选项 [D] The economic harm from illegal streaming（非法流媒体造成的经济危害），不仅体现了文章各段重复强调的主题词，即非法流媒体，也体现了反复提到的盗版所造成的经济损失，符合文章主旨。

这道题问的是文章强调了什么内容，属于典型的主旨把握题。很多同学一看到“is emphasized”就慌了，其实不用紧张——关键不是找细节，而是看全文反复在讲什么、围绕什么展开。

咱们通读一遍会发现，文章开头就抛出一个鲜明对比：正规流媒体平台“has struggled to turn a profit in streaming”（在流媒体业务上一直难以盈利），而非法平台却靠着偷来的内容“rake in about $2 billion annually”（每年狂赚20亿美元）。这个反差可不是随便写的，它其实在悄悄告诉你：问题的核心是钱——谁在赚钱？谁在亏钱？损失到底有多大？

接着往下看，第三段直接给出了具体数字：“costs the US economy about $30 billion in lost revenue a year and some 250,000 jobs”。注意，这里不仅提到300亿美元的收入损失，还连带说到了就业岗位的流失。这说明作者不是在泛泛而谈“盗版不好”，而是在聚焦经济层面的实际伤害。

2025-Traditional Reading-4-1.article:
Visit any antiques store and you’ll encounter artifacts from the past: photographs, letters, a brochure detailing the Sinclair dinosaur exhibit from the 1964–65 World’s Fair, the ephemera of history. Yet these objects aren’t truly ephemeral, because they’re still here, decades, even centuries later. Why? Because they’re tangible.

Have you pondered the life cycle of intangible formats, digital information, given that those who produce these artifacts seldom make provision for their long-term preservation? For millennia, we’ve known what we’ve known due to artifacts that have survived, often despite their original creators’ neglect. The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information. At the time of creation, no attempts were made at intentional preservation, yet analog materials have a chance of surviving and serving as the historical record that biographers, historians, and novelists rely on. Libraries and archives have traditionally shouldered the responsibility of organization, preservation, and access to information. Librarians digitize the tangible so that researchers the world over can quickly search and access their holdings. The result is an embarrassment of historical riches, which brings its own needle-and-haystack problems.

Librarians’ selfless devotion can act against us when users point to universality of access by holding up a cell phone and saying, “it’s all in here” as evidence that libraries are less vital for researchers today. Yet how was that universality of access made possible and, perhaps more importantly, how is it maintained? Who curates what is preserved? When it comes to born-digital information, the terrifying answer can be: if not librarians and archivists, then no one. Digital information requires a great deal more care than analog.

Even when a digital object is preserved, it may only be the carrier that’s saved, not the information itself. As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless. Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this? Without constant migration of digital assets, a nightmare about the foreseeable future is what keeps historians up at night: a historical record that abruptly stops when digital replaces analog.

As a librarian whose day job revolves around special collections and digital assets, I share the night terrors of historians, and I’d be lying if I said a comprehensive preservation solution currently exists. Yet researchers can take some comfort in the fact that there are a multitude of librarians devoted to discovering, organizing, and preserving digital information for researchers current and future. Librarians are uniquely positioned to understand how end users seek and use information. Thus we play an integral role in identifying, preserving, and providing accessibility to digital artifacts so that, while future researchers may find the digital realm a challenging place to ply their trade, they won’t find it an impossible one.
2025-Traditional Reading-4-1.analysis:
根据题干中的关键词 the artifacts from the past 可定位至文章1-2段。

1段1句：该句提及 Visit any antiques stores and you'll encounter artifacts from the past（探访任何一家古董店时，你都会碰到来自过去的人工制品），接着罗列了生活中常见的人工制品，并提到它们是短时效的历史物品（ephemera of history）。

1段2-3句：顺势提出疑问：但是这些物品都能够留存下来（still there），这是为什么？

1段4句：揭晓答案，即它们都是有形之物（tangible）。

2段1句：作者又提到了与有形之物相对应的无形式格式（intangible formats）的长期保存问题（long-term preservation）。

由此可见，作者在文章开头提及来自过去的人工制品是为了引出信息保存这一话题，吸引读者的兴趣。选项 [C] bring up the issue of preservation 是对作者意图的合理概括，与1段中的 still there、tangible 以及2段中的 the life cycle of intangible formats、long-term preservation 形成对应。
2025-Traditional Reading-4-1.tips:
这道题问的是作者开头提到the artifacts from the past（来自过去的人工制品）到底是为了什么。很多同学一看到“目的题”，就容易直接选看起来最顺眼的选项，但其实关键是要顺着作者的思路走，看他接下来讲了什么。

文章一开始说，你随便去一家古董店，就能看到各种老物件——明信片、旧海报、老照片等等，作者管这些东西叫ephemera of history（历史的短暂之物）。注意这个词，“ephemera”本身就暗示这些东西本来是容易消失的，可奇怪的是，它们still there（还在那儿）。这就引出了一个疑问：为什么这些本该消失的东西反而被保留下来了？紧接着作者给出答案：因为它们是tangible（有形的），摸得着、看得见。

但故事没停在这儿。第二段话锋一转，开始讨论intangible formats（无形的信息形式），比如数字文件、电子邮件这些看不见摸不着的东西，并且提出了long-term preservation（长期保存）的问题。你看，从“有形物品为何能留存”自然过渡到“无形信息怎么保存”，这才是作者真正想聊的话题。

所以，开头那段关于古董店和老物件的描写，其实是个“引子”——用大家熟悉的东西引出一个更深层的问题：信息到底该怎么保存？尤其是现在越来越多东西变成数字的、虚拟的，这个问题就更紧迫了。因此，正确选项应该是bring up the issue of preservation（提出保存问题）。

这里提醒大家一个常见陷阱：别被开头具体的例子带偏了！考研英语阅读里，作者经常先讲个生活场景或小故事，但重点往往在后头。你要关注的是“例子之后作者说了什么”，而不是例子本身有多生动。换句话说，例子是手段，观点才是目的。

2025-Traditional Reading-4-2.analysis:
根据题干中的关键词 digital objects 以及 tangible artifacts 可定位至文章2段。

2段3句提到：实体物品本身就是传递信息的媒介（The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information），这意味着人们可以直接通过接触这些人工制品来获得信息。

2段6-7句：该句提到数字化的信息：图书管理员将有形之物数字化，以便全世界的研究人员可以快速搜索和查阅馆藏资料（researchers the world over can quickly search and access their holdings），但浩如烟海的历史资料让人们难以快速检索所需要的信息。

从这里可知，数字物品传达的信息需要人们通过特定的技术或平台才能访问，而有形物品在传达信息时更为直接，因为它们不需要额外的设备或软件来解读。故选项 [B] convey information in a more direct way 与原文相符，是对2段3句The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information 的同义转述。
2025-Traditional Reading-4-2.tips:
这道题问的是有形人工制品（tangible artifacts）和数字对象（digital objects）在传递信息方式上的区别。要解对这道题，关键不是凭感觉选“看起来合理”的选项，而是回到原文找直接对比这两者的地方。


文章第二段正好讲了这个对比。作者先说，“实物本身就是传递信息的媒介”（The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information）。这句话听起来有点学术，其实意思很简单：你摸到、看到一个老物件——比如一本旧书、一枚铜钱——它自己就能“说话”，不需要打开电脑、登录网站或者装个APP。你直接接触它，信息就来了。


接着，作者提到图书馆员把实物数字化，是为了让全球的研究者能快速搜索和访问馆藏。但马上又指出问题：历史资料太多太杂，反而让人更难找到想要的信息。这里其实暗含了一个对比：数字形式虽然方便传播，但信息是“藏”在系统里的，你得会用检索工具、依赖平台，甚至可能被算法干扰；而实物摆在面前，信息是“裸露”的、直观的。


所以，正确选项说有形物品“以更直接的方式传递信息”，完全对应原文那句“The thing itself is the medium”。这不是主观推断，而是原文的同义转述——把“媒介就是物本身”换成了“传递方式更直接”。


做这类题有个常见陷阱：容易被“数字化=高效=更好”这种日常观念带偏。但考研阅读考的是作者怎么说，不是你平时怎么想。哪怕你觉得手机查资料比翻古籍快多了，只要原文强调实物的“直接性”，你就得跟着原文走。


小技巧：遇到比较类题目（A vs B），优先找文中出现both A and B的段落，尤其是带有but, however, while, whereas这类转折或对比词的句子——那里往往藏着答案。本题的定位句虽然没用明显对比词，但上下文逻辑已经构成了隐含对比，需要你稍微“串一串”前后意思。

2025-Traditional Reading-4-4.article:
Visit any antiques store and you’ll encounter artifacts from the past: photographs, letters, a brochure detailing the Sinclair dinosaur exhibit from the 1964–65 World’s Fair, the ephemera of history. Yet these objects aren’t truly ephemeral, because they’re still here, decades, even centuries later. Why? Because they’re tangible.

Have you pondered the life cycle of intangible formats, digital information, given that those who produce these artifacts seldom make provision for their long-term preservation? For millennia, we’ve known what we’ve known due to artifacts that have survived, often despite their original creators’ neglect. The thing itself is the medium that delivers the information. At the time of creation, no attempts were made at intentional preservation, yet analog materials have a chance of surviving and serving as the historical record that biographers, historians, and novelists rely on. Libraries and archives have traditionally shouldered the responsibility of organization, preservation, and access to information. Librarians digitize the tangible so that researchers the world over can quickly search and access their holdings. The result is an embarrassment of historical riches, which brings its own needle-and-haystack problems.

Librarians’ selfless devotion can act against us when users point to universality of access by holding up a cell phone and saying, “it’s all in here” as evidence that libraries are less vital for researchers today. Yet how was that universality of access made possible and, perhaps more importantly, how is it maintained? Who curates what is preserved? When it comes to born-digital information, the terrifying answer can be: if not librarians and archivists, then no one. Digital information requires a great deal more care than analog.

Even when a digital object is preserved, it may only be the carrier that’s saved, not the information itself. As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless. Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this? Without constant migration of digital assets, a nightmare about the foreseeable future is what keeps historians up at night: a historical record that abruptly stops when digital replaces analog.

As a librarian whose day job revolves around special collections and digital assets, I share the night terrors of historians, and I’d be lying if I said a comprehensive preservation solution currently exists. Yet researchers can take some comfort in the fact that there are a multitude of librarians devoted to discovering, organizing, and preserving digital information for researchers current and future. Librarians are uniquely positioned to understand how end users seek and use information. Thus we play an integral role in identifying, preserving, and providing accessibility to digital artifacts so that, while future researchers may find the digital realm a challenging place to ply their trade, they won’t find it an impossible one.
2025-Traditional Reading-4-4.analysis:
根据题干中的关键词 “ZIP disk” 可定位至文章4段3句，这是例子本身。由于论据服务于论点，当段落中间出现例子时，其所要证明的观点往往出现在上文中，因此，可重点关注4段1-2句。

4段1句提到：即使一个数字物品被保存了下来，也可能只是保存了载体，而不是信息本身（it may only be the carrier that’s saved, not the information itself）。

4段2句进一步说明原因：数字信息的载体可能会因为技术与格式的过时而变得毫无用处（As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete, the object is useless），让人无法读取其中的信息。紧接着，作者将 “ZIP 磁盘” 作为数字物品变得毫无用处的具体案例，对上述观点进行论证。

由此可知，4段1-2句是例子所证明的观点。故选项 [C] the po    ssibility of losing information in obsolete formats 是对原文信息的合理概括，其中 the possibility of losing information 对应 it may only be the carrier that’s saved, not the information itself，而 in obsolete formats 对应 a format becomes obsolete。
2025-Traditional Reading-4-4.tips:
这道题问的是作者提到 ZIP disk 的目的，属于典型的“例子作用题”。解这类题的关键不是盯着例子本身看，而是要往它前面找——因为作者举例子，通常是为了说明前面刚提出的某个观点。


回到原文，我们找到 ZIP disk 出现在第四段中间。往前一看，开头两句其实在讲一个更普遍的问题：即使我们把某个数字载体保存下来了，也可能只是保住了“壳”，里面的信息却读不出来了。为什么？因为技术在进步，旧格式会过时（As technology advances and a format becomes obsolete），一旦没人再用那种格式，那个存储设备就变得毫无用处（the object is useless）。


这时候，ZIP disk 就被拿来当“活生生的例子”：它曾经很流行，但后来没人支持了，就算你手里有盘，也打不开里面的数据。所以，作者不是在单纯介绍一种老古董，而是在用它来证明“旧格式可能导致信息永久丢失”这个风险。


选项里提到“the possibility of losing information in obsolete formats”，正好对应这个意思——不是说信息一定丢了，而是说存在这种可能性，而这正是前文强调的“可能只保存了载体，没保存信息本身”（it may only be the carrier that’s saved, not the information itself）。


这里提醒大家一个常见陷阱：别被例子本身的细节带偏！比如如果选项说“ZIP disk 已被淘汰”或者“人们不再使用 ZIP 盘”，听起来好像对，但那只是例子内容，不是作者举这个例子的**目的**。考研英语特别爱在这种地方设干扰项，一定要分清“例子说了什么”和“例子为了说明什么”。

根据题干中的关键词 best summarizes the text 可知这是一个主旨题，不能具体定位到某一个段落，需要串联全文内容，确定主旨。通过串联各段首句的具体信息可得知：

1-2段：介绍了有形之物和无形之物各自的留存形式，并暗示数字信息的保存较为不易。

3-4段：分别从日常维护和时代变迁两个角度，阐述了数字信息保存的具体难点。

5段：作者提到了图书管理员为历史信息的数字化所付出的努力，并指出这些努力将会为科研人员未来的研究工作保驾护航。

由此可看出，本文从逛古董店时会碰到过去的人工制品引出话题，阐述了数字信息保存的难处，并对未来数字信息的整理和储存对研究工作的助益进行了展望。选项 [D] Keeping digital historical records is a challenge（保存数字化的历史记录是一个挑战）体现了文章各段反复出现的主题词 “数字信息”“历史物品”“困难” 等，是对全文内容的合理概括，故为正确选项。
2025-Traditional Reading-4-5.tips:
这道题问的是哪一项best summarizes the text，也就是说要选出最能概括全文主旨的选项。这类题目不能只盯着某一段看，得把整篇文章串起来想一想：作者到底想告诉我们什么？

文章开头挺有意思，说我们在古董店里看到的老物件，比如旧书、老照片，都是有形的历史痕迹，它们虽然会老化，但至少还能摸得着、看得见。可到了数字时代，我们留下的信息——邮件、网页、电子文档——却可能悄无声息地消失。这里其实已经埋下了一个核心问题：数字信息看似方便，实则更脆弱。

接下来几段就具体解释为什么数字信息难保存。一方面，技术更新太快，今天存的文件，几年后可能连打开的软件都没有了；另一方面，日常维护也不容易，硬盘会坏，链接会失效，甚至整个网站都可能一夜之间消失。这些都不是小问题，而是系统性的保存难题。

不过作者也没一味悲观。最后一段提到，现在已经有图书管理员和档案工作者在努力把历史资料数字化，并建立长期保存机制。他们的工作虽然辛苦，但对未来的学者研究历史至关重要。这说明文章不只是在“吐槽”数字保存有多难，更是在强调：正因为难，才更需要有人去认真对待。

所以你看，整篇文章的主线很清楚：先对比实物与数字记录的差异，再分析数字保存的种种困难，最后点出应对这些挑战的努力和意义。正确选项必须抓住“数字历史记录”和“保存困难”这两个关键词。

选项[D] “Keeping digital historical records is a challenge”（保存数字化的历史记录是一个挑战）正好精准命中这个核心。它没有夸大其词，也没有只讲局部，而是用一个“challenge”概括了全文反复强调的困境与应对。其他选项要么太窄（只讲技术），要么太偏（只讲未来好处），只有[D]既全面又准确。

提醒大家一个小技巧：做主旨题时，别被某个细节例子带跑偏。尤其当选项里出现“only”“always”“easily”这种绝对化词汇时，更要警惕——考研英语的文章通常更倾向表达复杂性和平衡观点，而不是非黑即白的结论。
